pages.title: Timeline editing
pages.description: Complete reference for timeline tools, tracks, selection, snapping, trimming, splitting, clipboard actions, and hold frames.
pages.lead: The timeline combines visual, annotation, zoom, and audio tracks on one playhead. Editing rules depend on selection, clip type, project ownership, and available duration.

sections.title: Move, trim, and layer
bullets: Drag a clip to change its timeline start; linked recording sidecars move together until unlinked.
Drag the start or end handle to trim the active range. A clip must remain at least 40 ms long, and clips sharing a group ID trim together.
Dragging media beyond the current end extends the composition duration.
Drag visual track headers to change layer order.
Moving a visual clip into another visual row can also reorder visual tracks.
Disabled clips stay on the timeline but do not contribute to preview or export.
A multiple-selection change is applied only to selected clips compatible with the primary clip's property.

sections.title: Hold Frame
paragraphs: Hold Frame freezes the selected video at the playhead and extends the still portion as a timeline item.

rows: Enabled screen, video, or webcam clip with video media.
A compatible clip must be selected.
From start + 40 ms through end − 40 ms, inclusive.
Linked clips are split together, and the frozen segment can remain grouped with its audio sidecar.
Available from the supported clip's context menu.

sections.title: Imported-media failures
paragraphs: Dropped files are validated before import. Beam reports unsupported extensions or codecs, invalid or empty media, decode failures, non-local sources, and project-import failures. If an imported video contains unsupported audio, the video can be added while its audio is ignored.

notice.title: One import at a time
notice.text: A new drag-and-drop import is rejected while another media import is already running.

pages.title: Clip properties
pages.description: Complete reference for visual, webcam, blur, audio, text, and keyboard-caption clip properties.
pages.lead: The Clip panel follows the primary selection. Shared controls appear only for compatible clip types, and a multiple-selection edit propagates only to compatible selected clips.

sections.title: No selection
paragraphs: When no clip is selected, the panel shows an instructional empty state. Select an item on the canvas or timeline to reveal its properties.

sections.title: Crop a visual clip
paragraphs: Crop is a direct canvas editor rather than a numeric Clip-panel group.
steps: Select exactly one screen, video, image, or webcam clip.
Select Crop in the canvas toolbar.
Move or resize the crop rectangle directly over the selected visual.
Select OK to store the normalized crop on that clip.

notice.title: Single selection required
notice.text: Crop is unavailable without one compatible visual selection and does not operate on a multiple selection.

notice.title: Privacy effect
notice.text: The effect is baked into the exported video. Increase strength or use Opaque for sensitive information.

sections.title: Audio clip volume
paragraphs: This clip-level volume applies to selected system, microphone, or imported audio clips. Composition-wide and role-level volume controls are documented on the Audio page.
